item.title: North Dakota contributes to spacesuit, habitat development
item.description: North Dakota researchers have positioned themselves to contribute to space exploration as they are developing inflatable habitats in which astronauts can live and work on Mars and the moon. In addition, the team has created spacesuits for each celestial environment.

item.title: Coal expected to remain in energy mix
item.description: North Dakota researchers predict, in 50 years, coal will still make up three quarters of power generation in the state — but it will be “clean” coal.

item.title: Western water sources may supply eastern state demand
item.description: The future may see a swell of water moving west to east as groundwater wells near Washburn could be tapped to deliver water to Fargo and cities up and down the Red River Valley.

item.title: Society needs to choose another path
item.description: We all wonder what society is going to be like in five, 10, even 20 years from now. What expectations do I have for society throughout my lifetime?

item.title: Downtown may become hub to public transportation
item.description: While Bismarck’s rush hour may be no longer than a half hour, slow-moving traffic, jostling for parking space and fender-benders as the result of icy roads are not uncommon occurrences.

item.title: Airports prepare to handle additional passengers
item.description: In the years to come, North Dakota’s airports will see changes aimed at accommodating increasing numbers of travelers.

item.title: Disability and fixed bus route revisions proposed
item.description: Ridership and hours of local para-transit and senior bus service could be reduced by Sept. 1.
